title: 第七十章 疫气漫空生灵染 毒疠横行第九灾第六十九章 飞蝗蔽日千畴尽 寸草无存万姓穷
content_zh:
诗曰：
飞蝗去后野萧条，四野枯荒怨气飘。
腐秽熏蒸成疫疠，千家卧病哭声遥。
飞蝗席卷千里，田畴寸草不生，大地一片死寂。接连八重劫难轮番肆虐，村落残破、流民遍野，路上倒毙之人无人及时收殓，污泥腐草、尸骸秽气交织混杂，经烈日蒸腾，一股股阴冷毒雾悄然弥漫开来。
六道圣尊敛尽仙威，依旧以凡人身形缓步西行。一路所见，皆是面黄肌瘦、形销骨立的百姓，人人饥寒交迫，心神早已被无尽苦难磨得脆弱不堪。
何日抬手轻挥，拂开身前一缕异样浊气，鼻尖只觉腥闷刺鼻，不由得驻足吟道：
“蝗灾才过断生机，瘴气沉沉四野弥。
饥馁缠身人已弱，怎堪毒疠再相欺。
水旱风火山洪虫蝗，皆是伤及形体、夺人衣食。如今秽气凝结而成瘟疫，专侵脏腑、染传邻里，一人得病，全村遭殃，此劫远比诸般天灾更为阴毒难防。”
白洁凝神辨气，见远近村落上空皆被灰黑疫雾笼罩，眉宇间忧色更重，缓缓说道：
“八番劫难未抽身，毒雾横空又祸民。
诸灾尚有躲避处，瘟神一过少完人。
水火有形，刀兵有迹，蝗虫可视，唯独瘟疫无形无状，随风飘散，无孔不入。百姓本就体虚力竭，一旦染病，十难活一。此乃入世第九难，瘟疫毒劫。”
何月闭目静察天地气机，疫气缠缠绵绵，顺着风势四处蔓延，叹道：
“地荒物尽浊气浓，疠气滋生遍九穹。
纵使身强筋骨健，一朝染疾亦成空。
寻常疾患，可寻草药医治；这般天地大变而生的大荒疫毒，寻常草根树皮难以克制。我等封藏圣法，不施驱邪净瘴、起死回生之术，只凭凡俗手段，施救渡厄。”
公孙离望着前方村落炊烟稀疏，隐约传来断续**，怅然咏道：
“历尽千灾力已微，瘟魔暗里逞凶威。
村村户户皆愁叹，不见行人只见扉。

接连苦难之下，人心本就涣散，再逢瘟疫，难免人心惶惶，四处奔逃，反倒让疫气传播更快。稳住人心，便是当下第一要务。”
花月步道：“苦难层层加码，正是打磨道心之时。我们不通仙家疗愈之法，便学凡人行事，分隔病患、清扫秽地、熬煮草药、照料伤者。能多照料一人，便多存一分生机。”
黄鼬妖缩在衣襟深处，小鼻子不停抽动，被疫气熏得蔫蔫的：“这气味好难受，闻着浑身发沉。好多人都病倒了，连走路的力气都没有，这可怎么办呀？”
何年目光沉凝，环视四方，朗声道：“疫毒已至，避无可避。诸位分头行事，一者告诫乡民，分隔居所、断绝传染；二者清扫街巷、掩埋遗骨、净化周遭秽土；三者采摘山野寻常草药，煎汤分送，减缓病痛。恪守凡身本分，共历此疫劫。”
众人领命，即刻四散而行。
不多时，前方安乐村的惨状映入眼帘。往日村落虽屡遭灾劫，仍有烟火气息，如今却是户户闭门，街巷空寂。隐隐的**、咳嗽、啼哭之声，从一座座屋舍里传出，听得人心头发寒。
但见：
阴云惨雾锁村庄，疠气悠悠绕屋梁。
老少卧床身发热，亲朋隔巷泪沾裳。
柴门紧闭无人过，野径萧条少客行。
一染瘟邪全家病，十家九户尽凄惶。
药石难求饥又渴，残躯难撑命将亡。
大荒疫毒漫乡野，万里尘寰尽感伤。
村内早已乱作一团。起初只是两三户人家有人染病，不过短短数日，便蔓延至整座村落。染病之人先是浑身燥热、头晕乏力，继而咳喘不止、通体酸痛，卧床不起。村中本就缺粮缺水，更无医者良药，病患只能硬扛，轻症拖成重症，重症奄奄一息。
有村民强忍病痛，想要外出逃荒，可一出村落，便见沿途处处皆是染病之人，方圆数十里尽被疫气笼罩，逃无可逃，只得绝望折返。
“我浑身滚烫，骨头都像碎了一般……”
“孩子也染上了，这日子，熬不下去了……”
“到处都是瘟气，走也走不了，难道就要死在这里吗？”
哀戚之声此起彼伏，绝望如同潮水一般，淹没了整座村庄。
何日直奔村中最中心的街巷，这里病患最为集中。他大声呼喊，将防疫之法告知众人，声音穿透层层疫雾：

“疠气横行莫乱奔，分房隔舍避瘟魂。
勤除秽垢清街巷，且借百草缓病痕。
瘟疫最忌人群混杂，病患与健康之人务必分开居住。街巷之中的杂物、腐土、遗骨尽数清理掩埋，斩断疫气根源！”
他身先士卒，拿起农具清扫路面，搬运杂物，又协助村民在村落外围划分隔离区域，将重症之人集中安置，避免交叉传染。疫气萦绕周身，他只觉胸闷气短，却始终不曾停下脚步。劳作之余，望着满村病患，慨然吟诗。
白洁熟知草木性味，独自走向村外荒山野岭。山野草木虽被蝗虫啃噬大半，仍有零星寻常草药生长。她俯身采摘薄荷、苦蒿、野菊等可清热祛毒的野草，归至村中，指导村民支起大锅，添水煮汤。
content_en:
The poem says:
After the migratory locusts have gone, the fields are in depression, and the surrounding fields are deserted and filled with resentment.
The fumigation of filth has turned into plague, and thousands of families are sick and crying far away.
Locusts swept across thousands of miles, leaving no grass growing in the fields, and the earth was dead. Eight successive calamities have been raging in turn. The villages are in ruins and refugees are everywhere. People who have fallen dead on the road have no one to take care of them in time. The mud, rotten grass and corpses are mixed together. After the scorching sun evaporates, a cold poisonous mist quietly spreads.
The Saint of Six Paths gathered all his immortal power and still walked westward slowly in his mortal form. All I saw along the way were ordinary people with sallow faces, thin muscles, and emaciated bones. Everyone was suffering from hunger and cold, and their minds had already been weakened by endless suffering.
He Ri raised his hand and waved away a wisp of strange turbid air in front of him. The tip of his nose felt fishy and pungent, and he couldn't help but stop and chant:
“The locust plague has just passed, and all life has been cut off, and the miasma has settled all over the place.
People who are plagued by hunger and despair are already weak, so how can they be bullied by poison and calamity?
Floods, droughts, winds, volcanoes, floods, insects, and locusts all harm the body and rob people of their food and clothing. Now the foul air has condensed into a plague, which invades the internal organs and infects the neighbors. When one person gets sick, the whole village suffers. This calamity is far more insidious and difficult to prevent than all kinds of natural disasters. "
Bai Jie focused her mind to discern the energy, and saw that the skies above the villages near and far were shrouded in gray and black epidemic fog. The worry on her brows became heavier, and she said slowly:
"Eight disasters have not yet escaped, and the poisonous mist has spread across the sky and brought harm to the people.
There is still a place to hide from all kinds of disasters, and once the god of plague is gone, the human being will be perfected.
Water and fire are tangible, swords and weapons have traces, and locusts are visible, but plague is invisible and formless, drifting in the wind and penetrating everywhere. The people are already physically weak and exhausted. Once they get sick, it will be difficult for them to survive. This is the ninth difficulty of entering the world, the plague and poisonous calamity. "
He Yue closed her eyes and quietly observed the qi of the heaven and earth. The epidemic qi was lingering and spreading in all directions along with the wind. She sighed:
"The earth is barren and everything is turbid, and the turbid qi is thick, and the evil qi is spreading throughout the nine heavens.
Even if your body is strong and your muscles and bones are strong, it will be useless if you contract an illness.
Ordinary diseases can be treated with herbal medicine; ordinary grass roots and tree bark cannot control the great famine epidemic caused by the great changes in the world. We have sealed away the holy dharma, and do not use the art of exorcising evil spirits, purifying miasma, or bringing the dead back to life. We only use ordinary means to save people and overcome disasters. "
Gongsun Li looked at the sparse smoke in the village ahead and heard intermittent smoke faintly, and chanted sadly:
"After thousands of disasters, the power has been reduced, and the plague demon is secretly showing off its evil power.
Every household in the village sighed with sorrow, seeing no pedestrians but only doors.
Under successive sufferings, people's hearts are already distracted. When there is another plague, people will inevitably panic and run away in all directions, which will only make the epidemic spread faster. Stabilizing people's hearts is the first priority at the moment. "
Huayue Trail: "Sufferings are increasing layer by layer, which is the time to polish the Taoist heart. We don't know the healing methods of the immortal family, so we learn how ordinary people behave, separating the sick, cleaning the dirty ground, cooking herbs, and caring for the injured. The more people we can take care of, the more vitality we will have."
The yellow weasel demon huddled deep in his clothes, his little nose kept twitching, and he was wilted by the plague: "The smell is so unpleasant, my whole body feels heavy from the smell. Many people have fallen ill, and they don't even have the strength to walk. What should I do?"
He Nian's eyes were fixed, he looked around, and said loudly: "The epidemic has arrived, and there is no way to avoid it. You all work separately. One is to warn the villagers to separate their homes and cut off the infection; the other is to clean the streets, bury the bones, and purify the surrounding dirt; the third is to pick common herbs from the mountains, make soups and distribute them, to alleviate the pain. Observe your responsibilities as mortals and go through this epidemic disaster together."
Everyone took the order and immediately dispersed.
Not long after, the tragic situation of Anle Village ahead came into view. In the past, although the villages suffered from frequent disasters, they still had the smell of fireworks, but now every household is closed and the streets are deserted. Faint sounds of moaning, coughing, and crying came from every house, making people's hearts tremble.
But see:
The dark clouds and mist locked the village, and the misfortune lingered around the roof beams.
Young and old lie in bed with fever, and relatives and friends across the street shed tears on their clothes.
The firewood gate is closed and no one passes by, and the wild paths are deserted and rarely used by travelers.
Once the plague spreads, the entire family becomes ill, and nine out of ten households are in despair.
It’s hard to find medicine and stone. I’m hungry and thirsty, and my body can’t hold on to my body and I’m about to die.
The great famine and epidemic spread over the countryside, and the world was filled with sadness.
The village was already in chaos. At first there were only two or three householdsSomeone in the family got sick, but within a few days, it spread to the entire village. People infected with the disease first feel hot and dry all over the body, feel dizzy and weak, and then develop coughing and wheezing, body aches and bedridden. The village is already short of food and water, and there are no doctors and good medicines. The patients can only carry on, and the mild cases become severe ones, and those who are seriously ill are dying.
Some villagers endured the pain and wanted to go out to escape the famine. However, as soon as they left the village, they saw people infected with the disease everywhere along the way. The entire area for dozens of miles was enveloped by the epidemic. There was no way to escape, so they had to turn back in despair.
"My whole body is hot and my bones feel like they are broken..."
"The child has also been infected. I can't stand this life any longer..."
"The plague is everywhere, and I can't leave. Do I have to die here?"
Voices of mourning came and went, and despair was like a tide, flooding the entire village.
He went straight to the most central street in the village, where the patients were most concentrated. He shouted loudly and informed everyone of the anti-epidemic methods, and his voice penetrated the layers of epidemic fog:
"Don't run around when the evil spirit is running rampant. Separate rooms and houses to avoid the evil spirits.
Clean the streets and alleys diligently, and use herbs to relieve the scars of diseases.
The worst thing about plague is mixing of people, and sick people and healthy people must live separately. Clean up and bury all the debris, rot, and remains in the streets and alleys to cut off the source of the epidemic! "
He took the lead, picking up farm tools to clean the road and carry debris. He also helped the villagers divide isolation areas outside the village and place seriously ill people together to avoid cross-infection. The disease lingered around him, and he felt chest tightness and shortness of breath, but he never stopped. After working, he looked at the patients in the village and recited poems with emotion.
Bai Jie is familiar with the nature and smell of vegetation and walks alone to the wild mountains outside the village. Although most of the grass and trees in the mountains have been gnawed by locusts, there are still sporadic ordinary herbs growing. She bent down to pick mint, bitter mugwort, wild chrysanthemum and other wild herbs that could clear away heat and remove toxins. She returned to the village and guided the villagers to set up a large pot and add water to make soup.
